scout.name: Kane CLI Online Hackathon

prizes.other: Kane CLI swag for top 10 teams

scout.eligibility: Worldwide, 18+, individuals and teams of up to 4. Students, professionals, and independent builders welcome.
scout.notes: Focuses on agentic QA automation using Kane CLI. Requires a public GitHub repo and a 3-minute screen recording (no camera/voice required). Open to individuals and teams.

reasons: The candidate is open to non-students.
The hackathon is fully online.
Entry is free.
The first prize is $1,500 USD, which exceeds the $100 minimum.
Solo participation is explicitly allowed.
The deadline of 2026-11-19 is after the evaluation date of 2026-11-10.
The submission requirements explicitly state no camera or voice is required.

risks.risk: Prize payment logistics: International wire transfers or tax documentation (W-8BEN) for winners outside the organizer's jurisdiction can lead to significant delays or high intermediary bank fees.
Platform lock-in: The requirement to use 'Kane CLI' for agentic QA automation may involve proprietary tool limitations or undocumented API constraints that could hinder development.

builder.idea: Automated Regression Suite for E-commerce using Kane CLI: A self-healing test agent that monitors UI changes and automatically updates selectors in the Kane CLI configuration.
reuse: Existing boilerplate for Playwright/Puppeteer test scripts
Standard CI/CD GitHub Actions workflow templates
Previous documentation templates for README.md and project architecture
steps: Initialize Kane CLI environment and map target e-commerce site DOM structure.
Develop core agent logic to identify and report UI regressions.
Implement 'self-healing' feature: script that parses Kane CLI error logs to suggest selector updates.
Create a comprehensive test suite covering login, cart, and checkout flows.
Record a 3-minute screen capture demonstrating the agent detecting and fixing a broken test case.
Finalize GitHub repository with clear setup instructions and demo video.
demo_risks: Kane CLI API instability during high-load testing.
Potential for the agent to enter an infinite loop if the UI change is too drastic for the heuristic matcher.
Dependency on external site uptime for the demo recording.

scout.name: Codegeist 2026
scout.eligibility: Individuals who have reached the age of majority in their jurisdiction; teams allowed. Excludes employees and residents of specific restricted regions (Brazil, Quebec, Russia, Belarus, Cuba, Iran, North Korea, Syria, Crimea).
scout.notes: Requires a working Forge app or Rovo agent and a public demo video. Screen capture with captions is acceptable, so face/voice is not mandatory.

reasons: The candidate is open to non-students.
The hackathon is fully online.
Entry is free.
The first prize of $15,000 USD exceeds the $100 minimum.
Solo participation is allowed.
The deadline of 2026-12-22 is after the evaluation date of 2026-11-10.
The submission requirements explicitly state that face/voice is not mandatory.

risks.risk: Atlassian Forge/Rovo platform lock-in: The requirement to build specifically on Atlassian's proprietary Forge or Rovo infrastructure creates a high barrier to entry and limits the utility of the code outside of the Atlassian ecosystem.
Tax and compliance overhead: International prize winners often face complex tax withholding and documentation requirements (e.g., W-8BEN forms) which can delay or reduce the net payout.

Intellectual Property clauses: Corporate hackathons often include broad IP assignment or 'right of first refusal' clauses in their Terms and Conditions that may impact the builder's ownership of their work.

builder.idea: An AI-driven Atlassian Rovo Agent that automates cross-project Jira ticket synthesis and Confluence documentation updates to reduce manual project management overhead.
reuse: Forge/Rovo boilerplate templates from previous Atlassian ecosystem projects
Standardized UI components for Jira/Confluence integration
Existing documentation and video editing workflow for non-voice submissions
steps: Set up Atlassian Forge development environment and authenticate with a developer instance.
Develop the Rovo Agent logic to query Jira API for specific project status updates.
Implement a summarization engine using Rovo's LLM capabilities to generate weekly status reports.
Create a Forge UI module to display agent insights directly within Jira/Confluence.
Record a high-quality screen-capture demo with clear text-based annotations and captions.
Submit the app via the Atlassian Developer portal before the December 22 deadline.

scout.name: Enveda CASMI 2026
scout.eligibility: Open to Kaggle users worldwide 18 or older, subject to rules and US export controls.
scout.notes: A code competition focused on molecule identification from mass spectra. Participants must rank candidate molecular structures. Submissions are evaluated via Kaggle's platform.

reasons: The candidate is open to non-students.
The hackathon is fully online.
Entry is free.
The first prize of $16,000 USD exceeds the $100 minimum.
Solo participation is allowed.
The deadline of 2026-12-14 is after the evaluation date of 2026-11-10.
There is no requirement to show face or record voice.

risks.risk: Kaggle competitions often require winners to sign complex legal documentation (Affidavits of Eligibility/IP assignment) which may be burdensome for international participants.
High-stakes Kaggle competitions are subject to intense 'shake-ups' on the private leaderboard, potentially invalidating months of effort based on overfitting to the public test set.
US export controls mentioned in eligibility may restrict prize distribution to certain jurisdictions or require specific tax documentation (W-8BEN) for non-US residents.

builder.idea: Enveda CASMI 2026: Deep Learning for Mass Spectrometry Molecule Identification
reuse: Pre-trained GNN (Graph Neural Network) architectures for molecular structure representation
Cross-validation strategies for preventing leaderboard shake-ups
Automated feature engineering scripts from previous chemical informatics projects
steps: Perform Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA) on mass spectra training data to identify noise patterns and signal-to-noise ratios.
Implement a baseline model using a standard Random Forest or simple MLP to establish a performance floor.
Develop a GNN-based architecture (e.g., Message Passing Neural Network) to map mass spectra features to molecular candidates.
Apply rigorous cross-validation techniques to ensure model generalization and mitigate overfitting to the public leaderboard.
Optimize hyperparameters using Optuna to maximize ranking accuracy.
Finalize submission pipeline and perform sanity checks against the provided validation set.
demo_risks: Overfitting to the public leaderboard leading to a significant drop on the private test set.
Computational resource constraints when processing large-scale molecular candidate databases.
Complexity of chemical data preprocessing requiring domain-specific knowledge of mass spectrometry.
